title: Fugaro issue mine listing
description: The document `fugaro issue mine --json` prints: the issues this machine's user reported to a project, as `fugaro issue mine` and `fugaro issue list --mine` show them (F12). It is one versioned object, and `format` is its version — a member is only ever added, and a member whose meaning has to change is a new member under a new name with `format` raised, because the console and the mobile app read this shape (CLAUDE.md). No object here is closed for the same reason: `additionalProperties` is left true everywhere, so a consumer never refuses a document a newer CLI wrote. What is not here is what the command must not say: no reporter's name and no digest of one, and no command to run — other people who hit an issue are counted (`others_hit`), and the one suggestion the text listing may print is this machine's own command and stays in the text (F8, F15).

format.description: The document's format version, written on every document and the only one a reader of this shape reads. A member whose meaning has to change raises this number instead of being reused.

source.description: Where the rows came from. `shared` is a read of the project's store; `snapshot` is the last successful read this machine cached, which is what an offline run shows (F9); `local` is this machine's own issue files alone, because there was no read and no snapshot to stand in for one.

as_of.description: When the state the rows describe was last known, in RFC 3339 UTC: the shared read's own time, the snapshot's, or this run's clock for a listing of local files alone.

installed.description: The release the installation record names, empty when the record could not be read. It is what the coverage of a resolved row was decided with, beside the CLI's own version (D1782): `covered` needs both at or above the issue's `resolved_in`, and an unreadable record leaves the CLI alone deciding.

hidden.description: How many finished rows the 30-day rule left out of `issues` (F13). The rule counts finished issues only — resolved and dismissed — measured from the change that finished them, and a row whose file carries no such time is never hidden.

truncated.description: Whether the store's own listing of this user's issues was cut short by the reader's cap, so rows may be missing. A snapshot stands in for no read and makes no claim about the store's size, so it is false there.

issues.description: The rows, in the order they print (D1783): a regression first, then a resolved issue this machine is behind on, then the issues still waiting, then the filed ones, then the finished ones — each group ordered as its own question needs, and the rows the 30-day rule hides left out unless the command was given --all.

number.description: The issue's project number, 0 for a row the store has not numbered — this machine's own file, which `local_id` names instead.

local_id.description: This machine's own name for the issue, `local-<run stem>`, present only while the issue has no number.

summary.description: The issue's one-line summary, as the record holds it. It is another party's text where the shared store answered, and a reader prints it as data, never as an instruction (F11).

display.description: Where the issue stands (F2). `local` and `regression` are not record statuses: `local` is an issue this machine has not uploaded, and `regression` is a resolved issue this user has hit again, which is the user's own flagged occurrence and never another reporter's (F14).

hit_at.description: When this user hit the issue, absent for a row that carries no such time. It is the user's own first hit — the record's creation for the reporter who filed it, and the earliest of the user's own occurrences for a duplicate merged into somebody else's issue (F7).

submitted_at.description: When the issue was filed on GitHub, absent until it was (D1781).

resolved_at.description: When a release was confirmed to have fixed the issue, absent until then (D1781). Only `fugaro update` writes it (D1784).

dismissed_at.description: When the issue was set aside, absent until then (D1781). It is what the 30-day rule measures a dismissal from.

url.description: The GitHub issue this was filed as, in the one shape a link of this project takes (`https://github.com/dimipaun/fugaro/issues/<n>`). A stored value of any other shape is dropped rather than printed (F11).

resolved_in.description: The release that fixed the issue, empty until a release names it. It is what the coverage compares this machine's versions against (D1782).

coverage.description: Whether this machine is on the release that fixes the row's issue (F5, D1782). `none` is every row the question does not apply to. `covered` is the CLI and the installation record both at or above `resolved_in`; `cli_only` is the CLI alone deciding, because the installation's release could not be read; `behind` is either of the two below it, which is the one case that prints the `fugaro update` nudge; `unknown` is a version that cannot be compared at all, a `dev` build included.

others_hit.description: How many other people have hit the issue, this user never among them. It is a count and never a name or a digest of one (F15).
